On a phone sideways (short and wide): a rail on the left with the categories Model, Structure, MEP, Annotations, Views and Project, plus the views and the properties; the sheets open on the right.

Touch mode on a phone held sideways, 915 × 412

The tools are large tiles with an icon and a name. A tool still to come is greyed, Not available yet; a tool that does not work in the 3D view (Level, Grid, Reference Plane, the annotations) is greyed there, Not available in the 3D view. A tap on a greyed tile says why.

While a tool works, a green strip under the top bar shows its options and Done, which ends it (or finishes a sketch). While you draw a wall, Length… opens the command line: type the length of the next wall and, if needed, its angle, as 4.5 or 4.5 90.

A tap selects, and the selected walls show big grips at their ends. Over the drawing a floating bar offers Move, Copy, Rotate, Mirror, Properties and Delete; a long press opens the context menu. At the bottom left the view button shows the scale and the graphic style and opens Scale, Detail, Graphic style, Sun and shadows, Crop and Isolate Temporarily; at the bottom right Zoom to Fit.

docs.title: Gestures and the pen
docs.text:
Gesture What it does tap selects, or places the point of the active tool drag with one finger as a mouse drag: a selection window, a grip, an element long press the context menu two fingers pan; pinch to zoom; in the 3D view twist to turn the model double tap fits the view in the window

Pen in the top bar is for a pen: the pen draws and selects, fingers only move the view (one finger pans, two fingers pan, zoom and turn). A pen palette on the side of the drawing has Select, Wall, Door, Window, Detail line, Aligned, Text and More tools…. In a browser a pen is told from a finger by the browser; in the desktop app a touch that reports a pressure is taken for a pen.

docs.title: The interface
docs.text:
This chapter describes the BIMopen interface style, the one BIMopen starts in, on the desktop and in the browser. The other looks, the Classic style and touch mode for tablets and phones, run the same commands with the same names; Interface styles shows them and tells how to switch.

The BIMopen window with a wall selected in the ground floor plan

The window has these parts:

  1. the rail, on the left edge: BIMopen's mark, which opens the File panel, then Home, the contextual tab Edit, the tabs Model, Structure, Reinforced concrete, Metal, Prefabrication, MEP, Link and import, Annotations, Check, Massing & site, Collaborate, Views and Project, and at the bottom Settings;
  2. the tool panel, beside the rail: the groups of the tab chosen on the rail, as framed blocks of tiles;
  3. the top bar: the project and the active view, the command search, which is also the command line, the save state, Undo and Redo, the quick access tools, the light or dark theme, the ? menu and Options;
  4. the drawing area, in the middle: the views, each with its view selector at the top and the view bar at the bottom; while a tool works, the options strip runs over it;
  5. the element panel, on the right: the properties of the selection, or of the active view;
  6. the views and components strip, under the drawing area, which you can put away (F9);
  7. the status bar, along the bottom.

The panels keep their width whatever they show: a long name is cut with «…» and its tooltip shows it whole. Drag the edge of the tool panel or of the element panel to make it wider or narrower; BIMopen remembers it for the next session. A click on the tab already chosen on the rail folds the tool panel, and a second click opens it again. Without touch the interface is compact, to leave the drawing area as much room as possible; in touch mode the buttons stay big (see Interface styles).

In Arabic the whole window is mirrored: the rail and the tool panel are on the right, the element panel on the left, and the strips read from right to left.

docs.title: File panel
docs.text:
BIMopen's mark, at the top of the rail, opens the File panel: a full-window page with the file commands and the recent projects. In the Classic style File, left of the tabs, opens it; in touch mode Menu ▸ File. Back (the round button at the top) or Esc goes back to the model exactly as it was.

On the left:

Item What it does Projects ▸ Open… A page with Project… (Ctrl+O), IFC… and IFC Options… Projects ▸ New… Opens New project, with the template file to start from Components ▸ Open…, New… Greyed out: components are not available yet Recent Files The panel's start page, described below Save Ctrl+S Saves the project in its file; a project never saved asks for a name Save As A page with Project…, Template… and Options… (the save options) Print A page with Print… (Ctrl+P), Print Preview and Print Setup… Export A page with Image…, IFC…, Export plan SVG…, IFC Options… and Schedule… Open Documents The open view windows; a click brings the chosen one to the front Close Closes the project and goes back to the start page What's new in this version, Manual (F1), Commands and shortcuts, BIMopen website The links, at the bottom Options Opens the Options dialog Exit Closes BIMopen (desktop only)

The commands of the open project (from Save to Close) are there only while a project is open. Each page gives every item a line of explanation.

The File panel, Export page

docs.title: Recent Files
docs.text:
The Recent Files page has three bands:

  • Projects: the recent projects as square thumbnails, with the name and the date modified; a label tells which view the thumbnail comes from (3D, Plan, Sheet…). On hover come the pin, which keeps the project at the top of the list, the ⋯ menu (Open, Open as copy, Open folder, Copy path, Pin, Remove from list; also with the right button) and the ✕, which takes the project off the list: for a few seconds Undo puts it back where it was. The file on disk is never touched. A moved or deleted file shows grey, with File not found, Locate… to point to its new place and Remove; Remove missing takes them all off, Clear list takes off those not pinned.
  • Project templates: New project, the default template, the imperial template, the templates found in the files folder, the sample project and Browse… for another template file.
  • Components: the recent components (.bco, .bct), with their thumbnail and the same commands as projects. In the web version, files you open are kept in the browser (up to 1.5 MB each) and open again from here.

At the top, the search filters by name and folder, and two buttons choose between Thumbnails and List; the list also shows the folder, the date and the size, and sorts by name or by date. The choice is remembered.

Every save stores a thumbnail in the file: the default 3D view, or the view chosen in File Save Options ▸ Preview. A file that cannot be read shows a neutral icon.

At startup without a file the panel is the start page, without Back; at the first start, with the list empty, it offers New project, Open… and Sample project. In touch mode the thumbnails are bigger, the actions always show and a long press opens the ⋯ menu. In the browser there is no Open folder.

New…, Open…, a recent project and Sample project take the place of the open project; if it has unsaved changes, they first ask whether to save them.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The gear at the right end of the top bar, Settings at the bottom of the rail, or File ▸ Options, opens Options. It has, among others, these settings:

Setting Values Effect User Interface ▸ Language Italiano, English, Deutsch, Français, Español, العربية The language of the whole interface, at once User Interface ▸ Theme Light, Dark The colours of the window. Dark also turns on Invert background color. The sun or moon in the top bar switches it too User Interface ▸ Interface BIMopen, Classic The interface style, see Interface styles User Interface ▸ Touch mode Automatic, Always, Never The layout for touch screens, see Interface styles Graphics ▸ Invert background color on, off Views with a dark background and light lines Orientation cube ▸ Orientation cube size, Inactive opacity Small, Medium, Large; 0 % to 100 % The size of the cube, and how much it shows while the pointer is elsewhere Orientation cube ▸ Keep scene upright on, off Dragging the cube never turns the model upside down; off, the view can pass over the top Orientation cube ▸ Fit to view on, off A click on the cube also fits the model in the window Options, Orientation cube tab

BIMopen remembers the language, the theme and the style the next time it starts.

docs.title: Top bar and quick access tools
docs.text:
The top bar shows, from the left, BIMopen, the name of the project (a click opens Project information) and the active view; in the middle the command search; on the right:

The top bar Control What it does Saved / Unsaved changes The save state; a click saves, Ctrl+S Undo Undoes the last change, Ctrl+Z. Greyed when there is nothing to undo Redo Redoes the change just undone, Ctrl+Y. Greyed when there is nothing to redo The quick access tools The tools you added, then the arrow of the quick access toolbar The sun or the moon Switches to the light or to the dark theme ? Help F1, Commands (every command, in a window: The Commands window) and About (About BIMopen) The gear Options

Right-click a tile of the tool panel and choose Add to Quick Access Toolbar: the tool shows in the top bar and starts from there whatever rail entry is open. Right-click it there for Remove from Quick Access Toolbar or Add Separator (a line to its right). The small arrow after the tools, Customize Quick Access Toolbar, lists the default tools (Open…, Save, Aligned dimension, Tag by Category, Text, 3D View, Section, Close Hidden, Switch View): tick one to show it, untick it to remove it. In the same menu, Customize Quick Access Toolbar… opens a window with the tools in order: Move Up and Move Down move the one selected, Add Separator puts a line after it, Remove takes it (or a line) away, OK applies. The tools are kept for the next sessions.

Customize Quick Access Toolbar

? ▸ Help (F1) opens this manual, in the language of the interface, in the browser. F1 opens the page of what you are doing: the open dialog, the tile under the mouse (its tip ends with Press F1 for more information) or the active tool.

docs.title: About BIMopen
docs.text: ? ▸ About shows the program's mark and name, the version with the date and the commit it was built from (read when the program is built: a build in development says so), and the platform (the system and whether desktop or web). The note under it recalls that this is a test version. The rows open in the browser the Website, the User manual and What's new (the news of every version); Third-party licences opens in place the list of the works the program contains (typefaces, icons, the textures of the materials, the sky, the Moon and the stars), with their licences; the full texts are in the NOTICE file. Copy system information puts in the clipboard the version, the system, the graphics card and the backend in use: paste it when you report a problem.

docs.title: The Commands window
docs.text: ? ▸ Commands, or help typed at the command line, opens the list of every command. On the left the ribbon's tabs, in their order, then Modify and Command line only; in the middle, for each command, its name in the language of the interface, the name to type, its synonyms and its shortcut; on the right the description, the usage and an example of the command chosen. The search finds a command by any of these, in every tab (help door opens the window with the door already found). A command not available yet is greyed; Available only hides them. A double-click, Enter or Start starts the command as its button does; a command of the command line alone is written in the command line, to complete. Copy puts the command with its example in the clipboard. The arrows go through the list, Esc closes it. In touch mode the window opens from Commands ▸ List of commands (the command field with nothing typed), with rows the size of a finger.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
At startup, at most once a day, BIMopen reads from the website the file of the latest version (nothing else is sent). When a newer version is out, the bell in the top bar gets an orange dot (on the right of the title bar in the Classic style, in the top bar in touch mode). A click opens its panel: the version and its date, its main news, All the news, and Download and update, Later (no dot until the next start) and Skip this version (no dot until a newer one).

Download and update downloads the program with a progress bar (Continue in the background hides the panel, Cancel stops). Before anything is replaced, BIMopen checks the file: its SHA-256 checksum must match the version's, and the version's file must carry BIMopen's digital signature. A package that is not signed, signed with another key or altered is discarded and nothing is installed. Then Restart and update asks whether to save the changes, puts the new program in place of the old one and starts it on the same project and view.

  • Windows: the running program is renamed and replaced at the restart. Until the executable is signed, Windows may warn at the first start: More info ▸ Run anyway.
  • Android: Download and install downloads the package and the system installer asks to confirm (the first time it asks for the Install unknown apps permission).
  • Web: Reload loads the new version.

Without a connection, with an invalid signature or without enough disk space the panel says so and BIMopen keeps working as before. Options ▸ General ▸ Check for updates turns the check off; Check now checks at once.

The rail lists the tabs of the ribbon of the Classic style, with the same names and in the same order. Click a tab: the tool panel shows its groups as framed blocks, each with its name at the bottom, and in each block its commands in the ribbon's order, three to a row, as tiles with an icon and a name. A long name goes on up to three lines, broken between words or at a syllable with a hyphen. A tile with a small ▾ mark in its corner has a menu: a click on the tile starts the command, a click on the mark opens the menu with its variants. Resting the mouse on a tile shows what it does and, in brackets, the shortcut you can type to start it. The commands BIMopen does not run yet are greyed, and their tip says «Not available yet»; Level, Grid and Guide plane are greyed in a 3D view («Not available in the 3D view»). docs.title: The Model tools
docs.text:
The tools you use most to model are in Model:

Group Tiles Build Wall WA, Door DR, Window WN, Roof RF, Flooring SB, Object CM, Curtain Grid CG, Mullion MU Vertical Links Railing RA, Stair ST Rooms and Areas Room RM, Room Separator RS, Area ▾ (Area Plan, Area Outline, Area), Legend LG, Settings ▾ (Area and Volume Computations, Color Schemes) References Level: drawn in an elevation or a section, two clicks at the new level's height (from a plan it opens an elevation); Grid GR

Area Outline and Area work in an area plan: until one is open they are greyed, and their tip says to open an area plan first.

docs.title: The Annotations tools
docs.text: Group Tiles Dimension Aligned DI, Linear DL, Angular DA Text Text TX Detail Detail line, Filled region, Masking region, Detail component CD, Repeating detail RD, Insulation IS Tag Tag All TG The Annotations tools

docs.title: The Views tools
docs.text:
Views on the rail: the tools of the views and the Project Index Group Tiles Create 3D View ▾ (Default 3D View, Save View), Plan ▾ (Floor Plan, Area Plan), Duplicate View ▾ (Duplicate, Duplicate with Detailing), Section SE, Elevation ▾ (Elevation EL, Framing Elevation), Enlarged detail DT (a callout), Free 2D View VD, Schedules ▾ (Schedule/Quantities, Material Takeoff, Sheet List, Note Block, Predefined schedules) Sheets Sheet: a new sheet with the title block you choose; View: places a view on the open sheet Graphics Visibility and Graphics VG, Filters, View templates, Apply template to current view, Create template from current view Windows Switch View, Replicate, Cascade, Tile, Maximize, Close others, Panels, Drawing area theme

Sheets ▸ View works only while a sheet is open.

Save View works only while a 3D view is open, and Duplicate with Detailing only for views that are not 3D. Under the tools, the Project Index card holds the whole tree of the project.

Every ▾ menu also lists, greyed, the entries not available yet; the command search finds them all.

docs.title: The Project tools
docs.text:
Group Tiles Settings Materials, Project information, Styles by Category, Line styles, Purge unused, Project units UN, Snap, and Additional settings (Line styles, Fill patterns) Inquiry Check: checks the openings and references of the model and reports at the command line

Snap turns snapping on and off for the whole program: it is highlighted while on, as the Snap switch of the status bar. Additional settings ▸ Snaps… opens the Snap window: the length and angular increments, the object snaps and the overrides (see Snap).

The Project tools

docs.title: The contextual tab Edit
docs.text:
The wall tool at work: the contextual tab Edit in the tool panel and the options strip over the view

When you start a tool or select something, the rail chooses by itself the contextual tab Edit, drawn with a dashed outline, and the tool panel shows its groups under the name of what you are doing, in the accent colour: Draw Wall while drawing walls, Selection: Walls with walls selected, Multi-Select with elements of different categories, Edit | … in the other modes. When the tool ends, or the selection is cleared, the tool panel goes back to the tab you were on; Esc or a click on empty space does the same. A click on Edit shows its groups at any time.

It always has these groups:

Group Tiles Properties Properties: shows or hides the element panel; Type Parameters: the properties of the type of the selection, or of the next element the tool will place Modify Align AL, Offset OF, Mirror on Axis MM, Mirror on Line DM, Split Element SL, Split with Joint SG, Move MV, Copy CO, Rotate RO, Shorten/Lengthen TR, Shorten/Lengthen one element, Shorten/Lengthen several elements, Repeat in Series AR, Scale RE, Fix PN, Unpin UP, Delete (Del)

Delete works only when something is selected. The selecting and modifying chapter describes the Modify tools.

Other groups appear for what is selected or for the tool:

When Group and tiles Anything selected Selection: Filter (see Selecting and modifying) Doors or windows selected Opening: Flip facing, Flip hand Walls selected Modify Wall: Link Top/Base (the walls rise to the roof above them), Unlink Top/Base A level selected View: Open plan Sections or elevations selected Section: Split Segment (sections only), Flip, Go to View A callout selected Detail: Go to View Curtain walls selected Curtain Wall: Curtain Grid, Mullion, Panel Flooring or Roof tool Draw: Boundary Line, Pick Walls Stair or Railing tool Mode: Finish Edit Mode; Draw: Run or Lines Mullion tool Placement: Grid Line, Grid Line Segment, All Grid Lines A detail tool The drawing shapes of the tool The contextual tab of a selection

docs.title: Options strip
docs.text:
While a tool works, a strip runs over the top of the view: the name of what you are doing, then the settings of the tool. They apply to the next elements you place.

The options strip Tool Settings on the options strip Wall Height or Depth; the level the wall reaches, or Unconnected with its value; Alignment; Continue; Offset; Radius (greyed: curved walls are not available yet); Join at the ends and Automatic joining (greyed); Exterior on the left or Exterior on the right (the space bar swaps them) Door, Window Model on site (greyed); Tag on Placement with Horizontal or Vertical, Leader and its length; Loaded tags… (greyed) Object Model on site (greyed); Rotate after inserting: the object placed stays selected and Rotate starts Roof The shape: Gable, Hip or Flat; Slope, from 5° to 60°; Overhang, up to 2 m Stair Width, in millimetres; Railing Type, or None Dimensions What the cursor picks first on a wall: Wall centerlines or Wall faces Enlarged detail (callout) The scale of the new detail view, or Reference other view and the detail or free 2D view the callout points at (always on in a free 2D view) Area Outline Line or Pick lines; with Pick lines, Apply area rules or an Offset

The Ortho and Snap switches of the status bar work for every tool that draws lines: Ortho keeps the segments horizontal or vertical, Snap catches endpoints, midpoints and intersections. With Ortho off, holding Shift while drawing gives the same constraint; with it on, Shift releases it.

docs.title: Element panel
docs.text:
The element panel, on the right, shows and changes the parameters of what you are working on. Its header is one line: the type with its menu, and under it the family, the count of what is selected, as Walls (1), and Type Parameters, which opens the parameters of the type. On its right, Close (which clears the selection) and More actions (⋯: Type Parameters and the actions of the contextual tab). Under the header, its tabs; the rows of the parameters are low, with a wide column for the values:

The element panel: the properties of the view Tab What it holds Properties The type selector, then the parameters, in groups (Constraints, Graphics, Identification…). Click the name of a group to fold it. Values in grey are read-only: they are computed from the model. Apply, or Enter, confirms a value you are typing Materials For walls, floors and roofs: the layers of the type with their colours and thicknesses, and a preview of the layers Classification The category, the type and the IFC class Relations The level, the host, the doors and windows it hosts, the views and the schedules it appears in

The type selector is the header of the panel: a small preview of the type (walls, floors and roofs as their layers, doors, windows and components as a picture), the name of the type with ▾, and the family under it. Click it to choose another type: the selected elements change type, or, while a tool is active, the next element gets that type. The list opens over the rows: search the types by name; they are grouped by family, each with its preview. The arrow keys move, Enter picks, Esc closes the list.

The type selector

What the panel shows depends on the situation:

Situation The panel shows Nothing selected, no tool The properties of the active view (scale, detail, graphic style…), or of the view clicked in the Project Index A tool active The type of the next element, as New Wall, New Door… One element selected Its type and its instance parameters Several elements of one category Their number, as Walls (3) Elements of different categories Multi-Select, Common (5), and how many of each category, as 3 × Walls

Lengths are written and read in the project's units (millimetres in a new project). You can type a value with its unit, for example 2.7m.

docs.title: Project Index
docs.text:
Views on the rail shows, under its tools, the Project Index: the views, schedules, sheets and components of the project in a tree. Click ⊟ or ⊞ to fold or unfold a branch.

The Project Index Branch What it contains Views (all) ▸ Floor Plans The floor plans of every level, from the lowest, and the callouts drawn in plans Views (all) ▸ Area Plans (…) The area plans, one branch per area scheme Views (all) ▸ Sections, Elevations The sections and the elevations Views (all) ▸ Detail Views The callouts drawn in sections Views (all) ▸ 3D Views {3D}, the default 3D view, and the saved 3D views Views (all) ▸ Free 2D Views The free 2D views Schedules/Quantities The project's schedules, then the predefined schedules Sheets (all) The sheets, as number - name Components The types of the project, by category: walls, doors, windows, floors, roofs, Furniture, Plumbing Fixtures and the others; under a category of components, each component, then its types

The branches of area plans, sections, elevations, detail views and free 2D views appear only when they have something in them. The active view is written in bold.

With a view:

  • a click shows its properties in the element panel, without opening it;
  • a double-click opens it;
  • a right-click opens its menu: Open, Close (closes its windows), Duplicate View ▸ (Duplicate, Duplicate with Detailing), Apply view template…, Create view template from view…, Delete, Rename…, Properties.

The menu of a sheet has Apply view template to all views… instead of the two template items, and no Duplicate View. {3D} cannot be deleted or renamed.

With a schedule of the project, a click selects it, a double-click opens it, and the right-click menu has Open, Schedule Properties… and Delete. A predefined schedule opens with a click.

With a type, under Components, a double-click opens its type parameters; the right-click menu has Type Parameters, Duplicate…, Create Instance (starts the tool that places it, with that type) and Delete.

After a click in the Project Index, the keyboard moves in it: Up and Down go from row to row (the view's properties show in the element panel), Right opens a branch, Left closes it or goes up to the branch the row is in, Enter opens the view.

Views go on sheets from here too. Drag a plan, section, elevation, free 2D view, legend, saved 3D view or schedule onto the open sheet: its viewport follows the cursor and stays where you drop it. Or drop it on a sheet's name in the tree: the sheet opens and the viewport follows the cursor until you click. While you drag, the tree scrolls when the cursor nears its edge. The right-click menu of a sheet has Add View…. The views on a sheet are listed under it; the right-click menu of one has Remove from Sheet, and the menu of Sheets (all) has New Sheet…. In a 3D view the right-click menu also has Zoom to 3D Extents: the whole model, the elements hidden in the view too. A view already on a sheet is refused, with the reason on the command line; legends and schedules can go on several sheets. A saved 3D view is drawn on the sheet with the edges seen from its camera.

The right-click menu of a plan, section or free 2D view has Find Referring Views: the views that show its symbol and the sheets it is on; Go to View opens the one chosen.

docs.title: Views and components strip
docs.text:
The strip under the drawing area has three modes, chosen with the buttons on its left:

  • Views: live thumbnails of the views, grouped by All, Open (n), Plans, Sections, Elevations, 3D, Legends, Schedules and Sheets. The current view is framed, open views have an accent line. Click a thumbnail to open the view; right-click for the view's menu, with Open in the active window; drag it onto the open sheet, or onto a sheet's thumbnail, to place it there. + makes a new view: Default 3D View, Save View, Duplicate, Sheet or Schedule/Quantities.
  • Components: one preview for each type, grouped by category. Click a preview to place that type; drag it into a plan to insert it where you let go. A door or a window dropped near a wall goes into it, along it.
  • Commands: the history of the command line. Click a line you typed to run it again.
The strip in Views mode

On the right, Show filters the thumbnails by discipline and phase, the search box by name, and three buttons set the size: Previews, Compact and Hide.

The strip in Components mode

When the groups do not fit beside the modes, they fold into one menu, as All ▾. To give the room of the strip to the drawing area, put it away with Views strip, the last button of the status bar, or with F9; the same button or key brings it back.

docs.title: Panels
docs.text:
The element panel can move. Drag it by its header: it docks on the left or on the right of the drawing area, or floats where you let it go. The buttons at the top right of the panel dock it left, dock it right or make it float; Views ▸ Windows ▸ Panels shows or hides it and the other panels. Each panel stays where you put it in the next sessions.

While you drag a panel, only the places where it really docks are drawn, each as the panel it will become. The place under the pointer is drawn strongly, the others faintly. Elsewhere nothing is drawn, and the panel floats where you let it go.

docs.title: Dialogs
docs.text:
Every dialog opens in the middle of the screen, each time it opens, even if it was moved the last time or the window has changed size. Once open, it stays where it is: drag it by its title bar to move it. A change inside it, such as the Preview switch, does not move it.

Every dialog has a fixed size, which does not change with its content. The exception is the dialogs built around a long list or table (materials, visibility/graphics, object styles, filters, line styles and patterns, fill patterns, line weights, schedule properties, project and shared parameters, keyboard shortcuts, purge unused, IFC export classes, view templates): dragging one of their edges makes them larger, never smaller than they first open nor larger than the screen, and the list grows with them. They open again in the middle with the last size given.

docs.title: Drawing area and view windows
docs.text:
Every view you open is a window in the drawing area. A view opened again comes to the front; at least one window always stays open. At the top left of the view, the view selector shows its name: its menu lists the views and arranges the windows, and + beside it makes a new view. Views ▸ Windows arranges them too:

The view selector Tile What it does Switch View Lists the open windows; the active one is ticked Replicate Opens a second window on the active view, with its own zoom Cascade Overlapping windows, each with its title bar: drag a title to move a window, its edges to resize it Tile All the windows side by side, each with a title bar; the active one has a coloured title and frame Maximize The active window fills the drawing area; the others wait underneath Close others Closes every window except the active one Panels Shows or hides the Properties, the Project Index, the Command line, the Navigation bar, Keyboard Shortcuts and Recent Files Drawing area theme Each click switches the drawing area background between black and white; the rest of the interface does not change. It is the same choice as Invert background color in Options, and it stays for the next sessions

Click in a window to make it active: the tools work in the active window, the others only show the model. In Tile and Cascade, the × on a window's title bar closes it. Ctrl+Tab goes to the window you used before.

Tile puts the active window at the top left and the others after it, from the most recently active; Switch View lists them in the same order. Tile again after working in another window and that window comes first.

Options ▸ User Interface ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts lists the commands with their shortcuts. Search a command by name, or Filter the list (All, All Defined, All Not Defined, All Reserved); select a command, type the keys in Press new keys and click Assign. The same keys may go to several commands: typed in the drawing area, the status bar shows the first, the arrow keys go through the others and Enter or Space runs the one shown; Export… writes every shortcut to an XML file and Import… reads such a file back as your shortcuts (a file naming no command here is refused, and your shortcuts stay); Remove takes away the keys you added. Your shortcuts are kept for the next sessions and start the command when typed, as the built-in ones do.

A tool never changes the active view by itself. Started in a view where it cannot work (a roof or a room in a 3D view, a level in a plan, an area outside an area plan), it opens Go to View: the views that suit it, with the plan of the active level chosen first. Open View opens the chosen view and starts the tool there; Cancel leaves everything as it was. Edit Boundary of a floor, roof, stair or railing, from a section or an elevation, asks the same way for a plan of its level, and a new section or elevation leaves the plan you drew it in active. Move, Copy, a linear Repeat in Series and Mirror on Line also work in sections and elevations: along the view; the axis is the vertical plane at right angles to the view through its first point, however it is drawn. A radial Repeat in Series works in plans and 3D views: in a section or an elevation it stays chosen, but its clicks make nothing and the status bar asks for Linear.

docs.title: Views in separate windows
docs.text:
A view can leave the drawing area: Separate window in its menu (right-click it in the Project Index, on its thumbnail in the views strip, or on the title bar of a tiled window), or drag the title bar of a tiled or cascaded window out of the drawing area. On the computer the view opens in a system window of its own, which you can move to another monitor too, resize and maximise; on the web it floats in the page, because the browser opens no other windows. A view floating in the program also has System window, to move it into a system window.

You can separate several views at once. Each keeps its tools, its view bar and, in 3D, its orientation cube; the selection shows in all of them, and the active view is the last one you clicked. Back to the main window, at the top of the view, puts it back in the drawing area; a floating view also goes back when dragged onto the band at the top of the drawing area, which lights up. Closing the system window brings it back the same way. Where each separate view was stays with the project, and when it opens again the separate views come back to their places.

docs.title: Drawing in every view
docs.text:
A wall is drawn the same way in a plan and in a 3D view, on the level's plane: from the first click the wall being drawn follows the cursor, in the plan as its footprint and in 3D as its see-through solid, at its height and thickness; a dashed line carries its axis on, and others hold it in line with the points of the chain already clicked. The temporary dimension, blue with its witness lines and ticks, gives the length and the angle; type a length and press Enter to draw the wall that long. The snaps (endpoints, midpoints, intersections, perpendicular, other walls' faces and axes) work in 3D too. The wall selected in a 3D view shows, as in a plan, its temporary dimensions, the flip arrows and the ends to drag. In sections and elevations a wall is not drawn: Go to View offers a plan or the 3D view.

Roofs and floors are drawn in the 3D view too, on the plane of their level: Pick Walls takes the wall under the cursor (its top lights up in orange, Tab takes the whole chain), the lines are drawn with every sketch tool and with temporary dimensions, and Edit Footprint of a roof or a floor opens its sketch in 3D. Edit Boundary of a wall works in 3D on the wall's plane, and in a section or elevation that sees it face on.

While you draw or edit a sketch you can switch views (thumbnails, Project Index, separate windows): the tool stays active and goes on in the new view if it can work there. A chain of walls begun in a plan goes on in 3D from its last point, and a profile sketch begun in an elevation goes on in 3D. The wall being drawn and the sketch show in every open view at once.

docs.title: View bar
docs.text:
At the bottom centre of every view, a dark bar of buttons:

Button What it does Select and modify Ends the navigation mode, back to selecting, Esc Pan, Orbit (3D), Zoom With one on, the left button drags the view; Esc ends it Zoom to Fit Fits the whole view in the window, Home Zoom Options The zoom menu, see below The graphic style Wireframe, Lines, Shaded, Shaded with Edges, Flat Colors The detail Coarse, Medium or Fine Sun and shadows In 3D views, the sun and its shadows Crop Crop View crops the view to its crop region, or stops cropping; Show Crop Region shows or hides its frame Isolate Temporarily Hides or isolates elements or categories in this view until you reset it; framed while active Reveal Hidden Shows the hidden elements, to show them again Full screen The view alone in the window; Exit full screen comes back The view bar and the graphic styles

The scale of the view is on the right of the status bar, for example 1 : 100: it opens the list of scales; under Custom type another one, as 1 : 75, and press Enter. A sheet has no scale of its own: its views have theirs.

docs.title: Zoom
docs.text:
Zoom Options, on the view bar, opens the zoom menu: Zoom In, Zoom Out, Zoom in Region (drag a rectangle on the view; Esc gives up), Zoom Out (2x), Zoom to Fit, Zoom All to Fit (every open window), Zoom Sheet Size (the view at the size it prints), and Previous Pan/Zoom and Next Pan/Zoom, which go back and forth through the views of that window. Typed: ZR, ZO, ZF, ZA, ZS, ZP.

The navigation wheel is not available.

docs.title: Moving around in the views
docs.text:
In plans, sections, elevations and sheets Mouse wheel Zooms in and out at the cursor Drag with the middle button Pans Drag with the left button A selection window, or moves the selected elements (Selecting and modifying) Home Fits the whole view in the window In 3D views Drag with the right button, or Shift + middle button Orbits around the model Drag with the middle button Pans Drag with the left button A selection window, or moves the selected elements Mouse wheel Zooms in and out Home Fits the whole model in the window The BIMopen window with the sample house in the 3D view

A small tripod in the lower corner of the 3D view shows the directions of the axes: X red, Y green, Z blue. A saved 3D view remembers where you left it. On the selection, the move arrows let you drag it: drag an arrow to move along it, the centre to move freely in plan; the distance shows as you drag, and the release moves as Move does.

In 3D, the wheel zooms keeping the model point under the cursor in place, and the orbit turns about the centre of the selection, or about the point the view looks at when nothing is selected.

The Orientation cube, in the top corner of the 3D view, turns with the model. Its edges and corners are bevelled and every part is a target of its own: the six faces (TOP, BOTTOM, FRONT, BACK, RIGHT, LEFT, their names written on them in perspective and turning with them) look straight at that side; the twelve edge strips look from between two sides; the eight corner triangles from between three (an isometric view). The part under the pointer is tinted with the highlight colour, the one the view looks from now stays highlighted; a click turns the view there in a brief transition. Drag the cube to orbit.

The cube is light grey, its faces shaded by a soft light, in both the light and the dark theme; a compass ring at its foot carries the initials of the cardinal points (N towards project north).

The orientation cube

Under the cube the view's orientation is written: Front · perspective, Top – Front · perspective, Isometric · perspective, or Free · perspective when the view looks from no part of the cube.

When a face is seen straight on, four triangles round the cube (Turn up, Turn down, Turn left, Turn right) turn the view a quarter to the face beyond that side. The two curved arrows at the top right, Roll left and Roll right, turn the picture a quarter turn counterclockwise or clockwise.

The small house button at the bottom left, Starting view, goes back to the starting view; right-click it for Set as starting view, which makes the present view the starting one (each 3D view keeps its own, with the project). The small button at the bottom right, Cube menu, or a right-click on the cube, opens the menu: Orthographic / Perspective (for now the view is perspective only: Orthographic is greyed, «Not available yet»); Set as starting view; Zoom to Fit, which fits the model in the window; Options…, which opens the Orientation cube page of Options. Right to left (Arabic) the cube sits at the top left and the two small buttons change sides; the arrows stay where they point.

docs.title: The context menu of a view
docs.text:
Right-click in a view while no tool is active. If the cursor is on an element that is not selected, the element is selected first. The menu has, with a selection, the modify commands first (Move, Copy, Rotate, Align, Offset and the others), then:

  • Cancel: clears the selection;
  • Select All Instances ▸ Visible in View or ▸ In Entire Project: the elements of the same type; Select Previous: the selection made before;
  • Hide in view ▸ Elements or ▸ Category: hides the selected elements, or their whole categories, in this view;
  • Custom Graphics ▸ By category…: opens Visibility and Graphics on the categories of the selection;
  • Visibility and Graphics….

While a tool is active, a right-click opens the tool's menu instead, and the step in progress stays: Cancel (what Esc does, which still cancels the step), Repeat [command], Snap Overrides ▸ (the snap of the next point, as the two-letter keys do; in every view, see Snap), Zoom in Region, Zoom Out (2x), Zoom to Fit, Previous Pan/Zoom, Next Pan/Zoom and Properties. It is the same in plans, sections, elevations, 3D views and on sheets. With the menu open, Esc or a click in the view only closes it.

docs.title: Snap
docs.text:
Additional settings ▸ Snaps… (in the BIMopen style the Snaps… command) opens the Snap window, the same in both styles:

  • Snaps Off turns everything off (as the status bar's Snap switch, which stays as it was when the program opens again).
  • Length dimension snap increments and Angular dimension snap increments, each with its box: values separated by semicolons (by default 1000; 100; 10 mm and 90°; 45°; 15°; 5°; 1°). The zoom chooses the step: zoomed in, finer steps.
  • Object snaps: a box for Endpoint, Midpoint, Nearest, Work Plane Grid, Quadrant, Intersection, Center, Perpendicular, Tangent and Remote Objects, with their two letters; Check all and Check none. With Nearest off, the line under the cursor still offers its ends and its midpoint, even far away. Remote Objects (on at first) lines the point up, across or along, with the ends of lines far away, with a dashed guide.
  • Temporary overrides: the list of the two letters that hold for one point.
  • Restore Defaults puts everything back as it was at first.
Snap

The settings belong to the program, not to the project: they are kept between sessions.

While drawing from a point (walls, lines, grids, reference planes, sketches, and Rotate's second ray) the segment snaps its direction the same way in every view: horizontal or vertical, parallel or perpendicular to a line nearby, or a multiple of the angular increment the zoom gives; only when the cursor is a few pixels from that direction, otherwise the angle stays free. A dashed guide follows the direction, an arc with the value shows the angle, and the status bar says for instance Snap: Angle 30° · step 15°. The length is rounded to the length increment. Angle measured from, on the options bar, counts angles from the view's Horizontal axis or from the Previous segment. In the 3D view everything is measured on the work plane (the level's plane). At the command line snap {"angles":[45,15],"objects":{"quadrant":false}} changes the settings and snap alone shows them.

The anglesnap 0,0 3,0.02 command (also through MCP, and snap with two points) returns the direction a segment snaps to, by the same rules as every view.

At the top of the menu, Repeat [command] starts the last tool you used again; Enter does the same when no tool is active and the command line is empty. The menu is the same in plans, sections and 3D views.

docs.title: Command search and command line
docs.text:
The command search: commands, elements and views that match what is typed

Press Ctrl+K, or click the search box in the middle of the top bar, and type a few letters: the list shows the commands, views, sheets, schedules, elements and materials that match. Click a result, or choose it with the arrow keys and press Enter: a command starts, a view opens, an element is selected and shown, a material opens in Materials. The search finds every command of the tool panel, the contextual card's too (with a view selected on a sheet, «activate» finds Activate View), and runs it as its tile does.

The search box is also the command line. You do not need to click it: whatever you type in a view while no field is being edited goes there. Enter runs a keyboard shortcut (WA, DR, ZF…) or a command with its arguments (wall 0,0 5,0) as typed; Up and Down bring back the lines typed before. The log of what has been done, the commands run, their results and the errors in red, is in Command log at the right end of the status bar and in the Commands mode of the strip. The command line chapter describes the commands.

docs.title: Status bar
docs.text:
On the left, the status bar shows the project, the version and the active view, then:

The status bar
  • while a tool is active, what the tool expects, for example WALL next point [Esc to finish]:;
  • with no tool, the category and the type of the element under the cursor, as Walls : Exterior wall - Clay block 300 + ETICS;
  • while you drag, the length of the move, as Move: 1500;
  • otherwise the last line of the command log.

On the right: the coordinates of the cursor (X, Y, Z) in metres; the active level, whose menu opens the plan of another level; the number of selected elements, which opens Filter; the switches Select and Drag (drag elements without selecting them first), Snap, Grid and Ortho; the scale of the view; Command log; and Views strip (F9), which puts the views strip away or shows it again.

docs.title: Selecting, in short
docs.text:
The selecting and modifying chapter describes selection in full. The essentials:

  • click an element to select it; click an empty point to clear the selection;
  • Ctrl + click adds an element to the selection, Shift + click takes it out; Tab highlights the next element under the cursor, or a chain of joined walls;
  • drag from left to right to select what is entirely inside the rectangle, from right to left to select what it touches;
  • drag a selected element to move it;
  • Ctrl+A selects the elements of the open plan's level, or of the whole model in a 3D view; Del deletes the selection; Esc clears it.

On a touch screen the same is done with the fingers and the pen: see touch mode.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
BIMopen has two kinds of shortcuts: keys, such as Ctrl+Z, which act at once, and typed shortcuts, such as WA, which you type letter by letter. At the command line a typed shortcut waits for Enter, like any command; typed over the drawing area, it acts as soon as it is complete when nothing longer begins with its letters (see below). Typed shortcuts are the same in every language.

On macOS, Cmd takes the place of Ctrl.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key What it does Ctrl+Z Undoes the last change Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z Redoes the change just undone Ctrl+S Saves the project; a project never saved asks for a file name Ctrl+P Opens Print Ctrl+C Copies the selection to the clipboard Ctrl+X Cuts the selection to the clipboard Ctrl+V Pastes the clipboard: in a plan it follows the cursor and the click drops it; elsewhere, in the same place Ctrl+A Selects the elements of the open plan's level, or of the whole model in a 3D view Del Deletes the selected elements, and the elements they host Home Fits the whole view in its window F1 Opens the page of this manual about the open dialog, the tile under the mouse or the active tool F9 In the BIMopen style, puts the views strip away or shows it again Esc Cancels the step in progress; pressed again, ends the tool; with no tool, clears the selection Enter Runs the line typed at the command line; confirms a value in the element panel Up / Down At the command line, the lines typed before Space While drawing walls, swaps the exterior and interior side; while placing a component or a detail component, rotates it Shift While drawing, keeps segments horizontal or vertical (or frees them, when Ortho is on); with a click or a window, takes elements out of the selection; while dragging, frees a joined wall or keeps the move horizontal or vertical Ctrl + click Adds an element to the selection; held when a drag starts, places a copy Tab / Shift+Tab Highlights the next (previous) element under the cursor, or a chain of joined walls and lines Ctrl+Left Selects again what was selected before Left Right Up Down Move the selection a small step; with Shift, ten steps

Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+A, Del and Home act on the model only while you are not typing in a field: in a field they act on the text.

Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V act on the model while no tool is active (see Copy, cut and paste).

In a floor, roof, stair or railing sketch, Esc (or a double-click) also finishes the sketch when it has enough points.

In the Text Note dialog, Ctrl+Enter inserts the note and Esc cancels it.

Alt pressed and released, or F10, shows the key tips of the rail and the tool panel. With no tool active and nothing typed, Enter repeats the last tool. After a click in the Project Index, the arrow keys and Enter move in its tree.

docs.title: Mouse
docs.text: In plans and sections In 3D views Wheel Zoom at the cursor Zoom Middle button, drag Pan Pan; with Shift, orbit Left button, drag Selection window (left to right: inside; right to left: touching), or moves the selected elements The same Right button Context menu; with a tool active, the tool's menu (Cancel, Snap Overrides ▸…) The same; dragging, orbit Double-click Finishes a sketch –

docs.title: Typed shortcuts
docs.text:
Type the letters while no field is being edited, then press Enter. Without arguments, a shortcut starts the tool or opens the dialog; with arguments, it runs the command at once (see Command line and MCP).

With the cursor in the drawing area, the letters go to the command line (in the BIMopen style, to the search), and a shortcut acts as soon as it is typed, with no Enter, when no longer shortcut or command name begins with its letters: VR (cut heights), WT (tile), ZE, ZF, ZA, ZP, ZR, ZO, ZS, HR, HH, HC, IC, DL (detail line), RT (room label), TG (tag by category), TX, CC (copy), MV, RM, LL (level), RC (revision cloud), PP (shows or hides Properties), PT, RP, and the shortcuts you added. The others begin longer names and wait for the next letter, a space (arguments follow) or Enter: VG (vgsub…), HI (hide), DI (dim), AL (align), WA (wall), DR (draworder), UN (undo), MA (mask); so dim, wall 0,0 5,0 or WA 0,0 5,0 typed over the view run as typed. MA starts Transfer type; PT says in the status bar that it is not available yet; RP starts the reference plane. Typed in the command line itself, a line waits for Enter.

While a tool waits for a point, in every view (plans, free 2D views, sections, elevations, the 3D view on its work plane, sketches), two letters override the snaps for that point only: SE (endpoint), SM (midpoint), SN (nearest), SW (work plane grid), SQ (quadrant), SI (intersection), SC (center), SP (perpendicular), ST (tangent), SR (remote objects), SZ (close), SO (no snap); SS ends the override in force. They are also chosen in the right button's Snap Overrides ▸; those a longer name begins with need Enter. The status bar says so, and Esc or the point taken ends it. With several snaps under the cursor, Tab goes to the next and Shift+Tab to the previous. Shortcuts added in Keyboard Shortcuts under a snap's name work as its two letters.

docs.title: Modelling
docs.text: Shortcut Command Starts WA or W wall Wall DR door Door WN window Window SB floor Floor (the Flooring button) RF roof Roof CM component Object ST stair Stairs RA railing Railing CG curtaingrid Curtain grid MU mullion Mullion CP curtainpanel Curtain wall panel GR grid Grid RM room Room RS roomsep Room separator PA areaplan The Area Plan dialog CA areaboundary Area outline – area Area LG legend Color fill legend SC colorscheme The Color Schemes dialog

docs.title: Modifying
docs.text: Shortcut Command Starts MV or M move Move CO copy Copy RO rotate Rotate MM mirror Mirror on Axis DM mirror Mirror on Line AR array Repeat in Series OF offset Offset AL align Align TR trim Shorten/Lengthen SL split Split Element SG split Split with Joint RE resize Scale PN pin Fix: pins the selection UP unpin Unpins the selection MA matchtype Transfer type GP group Group: a new group of the selection SA selectinstances Selects all instances of the selection's types visible in the view DEL delete Deletes the selection U undo Undoes the last change

docs.title: Annotating and detailing
docs.text:
Shortcut Command Starts DI dim Aligned dimension DL lineardim Linear dimension DA angulardim Angular dimension TX text Text TG tag Tags the untagged doors and windows of the level – detailline Detail line RG region Filled region – mask Masking region CD detailcomponent Detail component RD repeatingdetail Repeating detail IS insulation Insulation

Note

Typed alone, DL starts the detail line; followed by points at the command line, it draws a linear dimension (lineardim).

docs.title: Views and settings
docs.text:
Shortcut Command Starts or opens SE section Section EL elevation Elevation DT callout Callout (the Detail button) DS splitsegment Split Segment of a section VD draftingview The Free 2D View dialog PP floorplan The Floor Plan dialog DV duplicateview Duplicates the active view VG or VV vg Visibility and Graphics WF, HL, SD – Wireframe, Lines, Shaded: the graphic style of the active view HH, HI – Hide Element, Isolate Element for now HC, IC – Hide Category, Isolate Category for now HR – Reset Isolate Temporarily EH, VH – Hide in view: the selected elements, their category RH – Reveal Hidden, on and off TL thinlines Thin lines, on and off SO objectstyle Styles by Category – material Materials UN units Project units PU purge Purge unused – filter Filters – viewtemplate View templates – applytemplate Apply a view template to the active view – linestyle Line styles – fillpattern Fill patterns – saveview3d Saves the {3D} view with a name – renameview Renames the active view

The commands with – have no short form, but their whole name works the same way. help lists every command and its short forms.

The zoom commands have typed shortcuts too: ZR zoom in region, ZO zoom out (2x), ZF zoom to fit, ZA zoom all to fit, ZS zoom sheet size, ZP previous pan/zoom. Views ▸ Windows ▸ Panels ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts gives any command shortcuts of your own (The interface).

docs.title: Openings
docs.text:
The Openings group of the Model and Structure tabs cuts holes that nothing fills: in floors, roofs and ceilings (By face, Vertical, Dormer), through several levels at once (Shaft) and in walls (In a wall). The five tools have the same names in both interface styles and in touch mode, and the command line runs them too.

An opening is an element of its own: it is selected, edited, moved and deleted like any other, and it goes where its host goes. A loop drawn inside a floor's, roof's or ceiling's own sketch is still an opening of that element's boundary, as before.

docs.title: Openings in floors, roofs and ceilings
docs.text:
Tool How it cuts By face Square to the face you pick: on a sloped roof the sides of the hole lean with the slope, through every layer Vertical Plumb, through the whole element, whatever its slope Dormer Plumb through the main roof, inside the outline picked from the dormer's walls and roof
  1. Start the tool in a plan (a ceiling plan for ceilings) or in a 3D view. Started in a section or an elevation, Go to View offers the plans.
  2. Move over the element: it is outlined in orange. With By face, press TAB to pick its underside instead of its top face (in 3D, the face you point at from below is the underside). Dormer offers only roofs.
  3. Click it. Sketch mode opens, Create opening boundary, with the Draw group: Line, Rectangle, Pick Lines and the other shapes. Dormer offers only Pick Roof/Wall Edges: only what can bound a dormer lights up (a wall's side face, the dormer's roof, a floor, an edge of the main roof). Pick the inner faces of the dormer's walls and its roof: the lines need not meet, the opening they bound shows dashed, cut plumb along the walls and back to where the main roof rises above the dormer roof's underside. It follows them when the walls move or the roofs change.
  4. Draw closed loops, then Finish Edit Mode. Open or crossing lines are refused with a message, and the sketch stays open.

A loop that crosses the element's edge notches it; a loop wholly outside cuts nothing and is left out, with a message.

A selected floor, roof or ceiling also has Opening ▸ Vertical in its contextual tab: the sketch opens on it at once, without picking it again.

docs.title: Shafts
docs.text:
Shaft cuts every floor, roof and ceiling between two heights.

  1. Start Shaft in a plan (or in 3D, on the active level). Sketch mode opens, Create shaft opening sketch.
  2. With Boundary line chosen, draw the shaft's outline as closed loops (Rectangle, Line, Pick Walls…).
  3. With Symbolic line chosen, draw the lines shown with the shaft in plans, for example its two diagonals.
  4. Click Finish Edit Mode.

The shaft starts at the level of the plan it was drawn in and reaches the next level up (with no level above it, it is 3 m tall). It cuts the slabs only within its height: a slab it stops in keeps the part above or below it. Walls, stairs, columns and components are not cut.

Every plan whose cut plane is inside the shaft's height shows its outline and its symbolic lines; the plan of a floor it cuts shows the hole. It is one element: moved in one plan, it moves on every level.

Selected in a section, the shaft shows as a see-through box: drag the arrows at its top and its bottom to change its height; near a level they stop on it.

Property Base Level, Offset at Base Where the shaft starts Top Level A level, or Unconnected Offset at Top Only with a top level Free Height Only when unconnected

docs.title: Openings in walls
docs.text:
In a wall cuts a rectangle through every layer of a wall, a curved wall included.

  1. Open an elevation or a section that sees the wall, or a 3D view. From a plan, Go to View offers the elevations and sections.
  2. Click the wall: it is outlined in orange. Curtain walls are not offered.
  3. Click one corner, then the opposite one. The rectangle follows the cursor with its size and its distances from the start and the base of the wall; the opening is made at the second click and selected.

On a curved wall the hole follows the arc. In plan the wall is cut where the cut plane passes through the opening, with no layer returns.

Selected in an elevation or a section, the opening has four handles on its edges: drag them to resize it; drag inside it to move it along its wall (it never leaves it). Moving, copying or deleting the wall takes its openings with it. For a round or polygonal hole use Edit Boundary of the wall instead.

Its properties are those of a shaft, plus Width and Height.

docs.title: Properties, schedules and files
docs.text:
Every opening has Comments and Mark, and shows Phase created and Phase demolished of its host, read-only. By face, Vertical and Dormer also show their Host and how they Cut.

Area and Volume of floors, roofs, ceilings and walls leave the openings out, in Properties, schedules and the material takeoff. IFC export writes each cut as an IfcOpeningElement voiding its host (a shaft gives one to each element it cuts); IFC import turns the openings no door or window fills back into openings of their floors and walls.

Visibility and Graphics lists Shaft openings, with Symbolic lines, and Openings among the model categories.

At the command line: shaft, wallopening, faceopening, vertopening and dormeropening (see Command line and MCP).

docs.title: Not yet in BIMopen
docs.text: Openings in beams, braces and structural columns, a strip foundation interrupted under a wall opening, shafts through toposolids and openings in roofs by extrusion come with those elements.

docs.title: Phases and demolition
docs.text: A renovation is drawn in phases: the existing state, the new construction and, when needed, phases in between. Every model element is created in a phase and can be demolished in a later one; every view shows the model as it is in its phase, with a phase filter that decides how new, existing, demolished and temporary elements look. One model then gives the plan of the existing state, the demolition plan, the design plan and the comparison drawing in yellows and reds.

docs.title: Phase statuses
docs.text:
The view's phase and an element's two phases give the element its status in that view:

Status The element… New is created in the view's phase Existing is created in an earlier phase and not demolished up to the view's phase Demolished is created in an earlier phase and demolished in the view's phase Temporary is created and demolished in the view's phase

An element created after the view's phase, or demolished before it, is not there in that view.

docs.title: Project phases
docs.text:
Project ▸ Phases ▸ Phases (BIMopen style: Project ▸ Phases…) opens the Phases dialog, with three tabs. A new project has Existing and New construction.

In the Project phases tab each phase is a numbered row, from the past (top) to the future (bottom), with Name and Description. A click on the number selects the row.

  • Insert before and Insert after add a phase next to the selected one, named in sequence (Phase 1, Phase 2…). Phases cannot be reordered: insert them in the right place.
  • Combine with ▸ Previous or Next removes the selected phase: the elements, views, schedules and rooms that used it move to the phase it is combined with.

Names cannot be empty or repeated. OK applies the three tabs together, as one step that Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes back; the dialog's Cancel changes nothing. The Preview switch in the header shows the active view with the changes not yet confirmed, with the filter chosen under the preview.

docs.title: Phase filters
docs.text:
In the Phase filters tab each filter says, for each status (New, Existing, Demolished, Temporary), whether its elements are drawn By category (as the view's styles and overrides say), Overridden (with the status's graphic overrides) or Do not display (not drawn, not selectable).

Default filter New Existing Demolished Temporary Show all By category Overridden Overridden Overridden Show demolished + new By category Do not display Overridden Overridden Show new By category Do not display Do not display Do not display Show previous + demolished Do not display By category Overridden Do not display Show previous + new By category By category Do not display Do not display Show previous phase Do not display Overridden Overridden Do not display Yellows and reds Overridden Overridden Overridden Do not display

New adds a filter (everything by category), Delete removes it: when a view uses it the dialog asks first, and those views go to None. In the first phase Show previous phase shows nothing. To see everything without overrides, choose None as the view's filter.

docs.title: Graphic overrides
docs.text:
The Graphic overrides tab has a row per status: Projection lines and Cut lines (weight, colour, line pattern), Surface Patterns and Cut patterns (visible, pattern, colour; Clear overrides returns to the category's), Halftone (lines, patterns and fills blended towards the background, not the material colours of shaded views) and Material (its shaded colour and appearance in shaded and realistic views).

They apply where a filter says Overridden. The view's filters and the graphics by element win over them. The defaults follow the Italian practice: existing grey, demolished yellow and dashed, new red, temporary dotted in halftone.

docs.title: The phase of views
docs.text:
Plans, ceiling plans, sections, elevations, 3D views, area plans and schedules have Phase filter and Phase in the Phases group of their properties. A new view takes the last phase and Show all; Duplicate view keeps phase and filter, then each can change: the same floor at two moments. A view template can set the filter (Phase filter among the included properties), never the phase.

In the BIMopen style the Phase · Filter chip at the top of the view opens a menu that changes either.

docs.title: The phases of elements
docs.text:
Every model element (walls, doors, windows, components, floors, roofs, ceilings, columns, stairs, railings, ramps, curtain walls) has in the Phases group of its properties:

  • Phase created: that of the view it was created (or pasted) in;
  • Phase demolished: None, or the phase it is demolished in; only the phase created and the later ones are offered, and None undoes the demolition.

Annotations, dimensions, texts and detail items have no phases: they belong to their view. The sub-walls of a stacked wall and the pieces of a curved wall follow the whole wall. Earlier projects, with the two fixed phases of walls, open with the phases of the same names.

docs.title: Demolish
docs.text:
Modify ▸ Shapes ▸ Demolish (BIMopen style: Modify ▸ Demolish) works in plans, sections, elevations and 3D views. A hammer appears beside the cursor and what can be demolished in the view's phase is highlighted. A click demolishes the element in that phase, in every view of the same phase:

  • a demolished wall takes its doors and windows with it;
  • an element created in the same phase becomes temporary;
  • when the view's filter does not show demolitions, the element disappears at once.

With elements already selected, Demolish demolishes them all at once, then waits for more clicks. Esc or Modify close the tool; each click is one undo step.

docs.title: Infills
docs.text:
Where a door or window is demolished and its wall stays, the hole is filled from the demolition's phase on, with the wall's layers: it shows in plan, section, elevation and 3D. Where an opening is made in a later phase than its wall, the wall is whole in the earlier phases.

An infill is selected with a click, for instance in a section with Show previous + new: its Type can be another basic wall type, to draw a different infilling; the infill of the phases before the opening always has the wall's structure. Infills cannot be moved, rotated, mirrored, copied or pasted: they follow their openings.

docs.title: Rooms and schedules by phase
docs.text:
A room belongs to the phase of the view it is placed in (its Phase is read only): a plan shows, tags and selects only the rooms of its phase, and the same number can exist in different phases. A room is bounded by what exists at the end of its phase: demolishing a partition changes the rooms of that phase and the later ones, not those of the existing state. Copy to clipboard a room from a view and Paste in the active view in a view of another phase: the room goes to that phase with the same properties.

A schedule has Phase and Phase filter as views do (in New schedule the last phase is proposed): its rows are the elements as they are in that phase, those the filter shows. Show previous + demolished lists the doors to remove, Show new those to buy. The fields Phase created and Phase demolished can be shown, sorted, filtered and edited in the cell.

View filters have rules on Phase created and Phase demolished: equal or not, and less than / greater than for earlier or later in the phases' order.

docs.title: Phase legends
docs.text: A legend component has the Phase status property: with Existing, Demolished, New or Temporary the sample is drawn with that status's overrides, beside its text.

docs.title: Exchange
docs.text:
• IFC: with a phased project, Export ▸ IFC asks the Phase to export (the last one is proposed). The elements that exist in that phase are written, each with its status (Status: NEW, EXISTING, DEMOLISH, TEMPORARY) in its class's common property set and its two phases by name. When an IFC file is opened, objects with this status take the matching phases of the project.
  • DWG and DXF: in Export CAD formats the option Phase status in the layer name adds the status's suffix to the category's layer (-EXST, -DEMO, -NEWW, -TEMP): a demolished wall goes on A-WALL-DEMO.

Phase mapping of linked models will come with linked models.

docs.title: Projects and files
docs.text:
This chapter describes how a project is created, opened, saved and exchanged with other programs, its settings and the options of BIMopen itself.

The File panel, on BIMopen's mark

docs.title: Creating a project
docs.text:
File ➤ New… opens New project:

  • Template file: BIMopen's default template, or the one set in Options ➤ File Locations; the BIMopen imperial template (see Imperial units); a template file chosen with Browse…; or None, which starts from two levels and one type of each kind and asks for the system of measurement: Imperial or Metric.
  • Create new: Project or Project Template.
New project

A project made from a template has everything the template had: types, settings, views, sheets, project information and print settings. Saving it asks for a name, so the template is not overwritten.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: A template is a .bpt file. File ➤ Save As ➤ Template… saves the open project as a template; a project created as a Project Template, or a template opened, is saved as a template too.

docs.title: BIMopen files
docs.text:
BIMopen saves in its own format, format 2027, with four extensions:

Extension What it is .bpr A project .bpt A project template, which new projects start from .bco A component, loaded into projects .bct A component template, which new components start from

The format is made so that every file of format 2027 also opens in later versions of BIMopen. Every element has a permanent identifier, saved in the file, which IFC export uses as its GlobalId: the same element has the same GlobalId in every export, and a copy gets a new one.

A file that is not of format 2027 does not open, and the command line says why: it is not a BIMopen file, or it was saved with a newer version of BIMopen, whose number it gives. Models are exchanged with other programs in IFC: see Import and conversion.

docs.title: Opening a project
docs.text:
Ctrl+O or File ➤ Open… ➤ Project… opens a project. File shows the recent projects as thumbnails, the most recent first; a pin keeps a project at the top of the list, the ✕ takes it off the list (the file stays where it is) and a moved file is found again with Locate… (see Recent Files). Without a file, BIMopen starts on the File panel (unless Enable Recent Files page at startup is unticked in the options). Dropping a project file on the window opens it too.

Recent projects in the File panel

A project already open in another BIMopen window opens read-only: Save asks for a new name. If BIMopen stopped without saving (a crash, a power cut), opening the project again brings the unsaved work back as unsaved changes.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Ctrl+S, or a click on the save state in the top bar, saves the project; until then the file stays as it was last saved, and the top bar says Unsaved changes. File ➤ Save As ➤ Project… writes it to a new file and goes on there.

Save As ➤ Options… opens File Save Options: Maximum backups keeps that many earlier versions beside the file (house.0001.bpr, house.0002.bpr…), deleting the oldest; Compact file rewrites the file without its obsolete parts at the next save; Preview chooses the view of the thumbnail that every save stores in the file and that the File panel shows: the Default 3D View, the Active view or a chosen view.

When a changed project stays unsaved for the interval set in Options ➤ General (Save reminder interval, 30 minutes to start with), Save Reminder offers to save it, not to save it, or to change the interval.

One project is open at a time: the project opened takes the place of the one open, and the views of that one close with it. Opening the project already open leaves it as it is, when it has no unsaved changes; with changes, answering No to the question to save them drops them and opens the file again as last saved, as closing it without saving and reopening it.

Before New, Open…, a recent document, a dropped file, open at the command line, the sample project, or closing the window, a changed project asks Save changes to …?: Yes saves it, No drops the changes, Cancel keeps it open.

In the browser, Open… uses the browser's file chooser, and Save downloads the file; backups, crash recovery and read-only opening need a file on disk and are desktop-only.

docs.title: Saving for archiving
docs.text: The project file keeps a cache of the views slow to make again (elevations, sections and thumbnails taking 300 ms or more): reopened, it shows them at once. It holds only for the same model, language and BIMopen version; otherwise it is dropped by itself, and the file opens the same without it. Save As ➤ For archiving… saves a compressed copy without the cache, smaller, to hand over or archive: the copy makes those views again the first time, and the open project stays on its file. Options ➤ Use the view cache in the project file, turned off, removes it at the ordinary save too.

docs.title: Project information
docs.text: Settings ➤ Settings ➤ Project information sets the project's name, number, client, address, issue date and status: the title blocks of every sheet show them.

docs.title: Project units
docs.text:
Settings ➤ Settings ➤ Project units lists the quantities (length, area, volume, angle, slope and the others) with a sample of each, and the Decimal symbol/digit grouping. Format… of a quantity sets its unit, its Rounding (a number of decimals, or Custom with an Increment factor, such as 5 mm), its Unit symbol, Suppress trailing zeros, the plus sign for positive values and digit grouping.

Project units, then Format… of a quantity

docs.title: Imperial units
docs.text:
In Format… the units of a length are in two groups, Metric and Imperial: Feet and fractional inches (5' - 6 1/2"), Fractional inches (66 1/2"), Decimal feet and Decimal inches. Areas can be in Square feet, Square inches or Acres, volumes in Cubic feet, Cubic inches or Cubic yards, slopes as Rise/12" or as a ratio. With fractions, Rounding is to the nearest inch or to the nearest 1/2" to 1/256"; a value that rounds up to 12" is carried into the feet: at 1/16", 11 63/64" reads 1' - 0". Suppress 0 feet writes 4" for 0' - 4", Remove spaces writes 1'-2" for 1' - 2", and Unit symbol chooses between ' and ft, or ft² and SF. Other values shows the format on a few more values.

A schedule field's Field Format… and a dimension type's Units Format have the same fields, besides Use project settings: a takeoff can give volumes in cubic yards in a project in cubic feet, and a dimension type for details can round to 1/32" where the plans round to 1/16".

The model is kept in metres: changing the units changes how values are shown and typed, never the geometry. Switching a project from metric to imperial and back leaves every element where it was.

Project units in feet and inches

In a project in feet and inches the view scales are the architectural ones, from 12" = 1'-0" to 3/64" = 1'-0", and the engineering ones, from 1" = 10'-0" to 1" = 100'-0": in the view bar, in the Properties and on sheets. A scale that is neither shows as a ratio.

Scale Ratio Typical use 12" = 1'-0" 1:1 full-size details 6" = 1'-0" 1:2 complex joints and nodes 3" = 1'-0" 1:4 masonry and joinery details 1 1/2" = 1'-0" 1:8 component and window details 1" = 1'-0" 1:12 standard construction details 3/4" = 1'-0" 1:16 structural nodes 1/2" = 1'-0" 1:24 wall sections and partial elevations 3/8" = 1'-0" 1:32 kitchen and bathroom plans, enlarged details 1/4" = 1'-0" 1:48 the architectural standard for plans and sections 1/8" = 1'-0" 1:96 the engineering and MEP standard, general plans 3/32" = 1'-0" 1:128 large commercial plans 1/16" = 1'-0" 1:192 key plans and general layouts 3/64" = 1'-0" 1:256 very large site plans 1" = 10'-0" 1:120 civil engineering and site plans 1" = 20'-0" 1:240 subdivision plans 1" = 30'-0" 1:360 civil works and utilities 1" = 40'-0" 1:480 topography and road surveys 1" = 50'-0" 1:600 urban planning and context plans 1" = 60'-0" 1:720 territorial surveys 1" = 100'-0" 1:1200 cadastral maps A plan at 1/4" = 1'-0", dimensioned to 1/16" A schedule in feet and inches

The BIMopen imperial template has the same set of types as the metric one, in US trade sizes: walls of 2x4 and 2x6 wood studs, of 8" blocks and brick, of metal studs; doors from 30" to 36" x 80"; windows with a 3'-0" sill; stairs with risers of at most 7 3/4" and treads of at least 10"; railings 36" and 42" high. Lengths and dimensions are rounded to 1/32", the length dimension snap increments are 4', 1', 6" and 1", the work plane grid is 4', plans are at 1/8" = 1'-0" and text is 3/32" and 1/8" high. These are starting points: each one can be changed in the project. Changing the units of a project does not rename its types.

Tip: to keep drawings readable on site, give the dimension types a coarser rounding: in a dimension type's Type Parameters, Units Format opens Format; untick Use project settings and round to 1/16" or 1/8".

A new project from no template asks for the system of measurement

docs.title: Typing lengths
docs.text:
A length typed in the Properties, on a temporary dimension, in the options strip, in a dialog or at the command line is read this way:

  • with a unit, in that unit, in any project: 300mm, 1.2 m, 1 m 20 cm, 6", 5.5', 5.5 ft;
  • feet and inches: 5'6", 5' 6 1/2", 5'-6 1/2"; after the feet the last " can be left out (5'6), and inches from 12 up are carried into the feet (5' 14" is 6'-2");
  • a number without a unit is in the project's unit of length; in a project in feet, two numbers are feet and inches: 8 6 is 8'-6", 8 6 1/2 is 8'-6 1/2";
  • fractions are of an inch; a fraction of a foot is written as a decimal (5.5');
  • after =, a formula: =10' + 6", =12'/5, =3000mm/2; its numbers without a unit are in the project's unit.

The decimal symbol is the project's. While a value is being edited it is shown at full precision (to 1/256" in feet and inches), so confirming it unchanged changes nothing. At the command line a number without a unit is in metres in a metric project and in feet in a project in feet and inches; a length can always carry its unit: wall 0,0 20',0.

docs.title: Sun Settings
docs.text: Settings ➤ Additional settings ➤ Sun Settings opens the sun settings of the active view, the same as the sun button of the view control bar (see Views and graphics).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
File ➤ Options has four tabs; the choices are kept between sessions.

Tab What it sets General The save reminder interval User Interface The theme (Light or Dark), the language, the interface style and size; Enable Recent Files page at startup; in the Classic style, the ribbon tab after a selection ends or a tool closes (Stay on the Modify tab or Return to the previous tab) and Display the contextual tab on selection; Tooltip Assistance (None, Minimal, Normal, Extra High) Graphics Hardware acceleration, Graphics card and the In use line, 3D view ▸ Edges, Use anti-aliasing for 3D views, Invert background color, Selection color, Highlight color, Temporary Dimension Text Appearance (size and background) File Locations Default template file path (the template of New) and Default path for user files (where the file dialogs open) Options, User Interface tab

docs.title: Graphics: graphics card and edges
docs.text:
